item.title: U.S. reports highest number of measles cases in 35 years
item.description: For the second year in a row, the U.S. has reported a record-breaking number of measles cases. The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention on Friday said the country has now confirmed 2,318 measles cases -- the highest case count since 1991.
item.content:encoded: For the second year in a row, the U.S. has reported a record-breaking number of measles cases. The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention on Friday said the country has now confirmed 2,318 measles cases -- the highest case count since 1991.
item.dc:creator: Maria Godoy

item.title: 15 years later, is the FDA's produce safety overhaul working?
item.description: Fifteen years ago, the FDA overhauled its safety rules for fruits and vegetables, hoping to prevent outbreaks of foodborne illness. How's that system working today?

item.title: FDA panel backs easier access to peptides
item.description: Advisers to the Food and Drug Administration are backing popular peptide therapies. They voted to allow specialized pharmacies to make them despite agency scientists' recommendations against it.

item.title: A doctor shares how much sleep people need to function through the day
item.description: Japan's prime minister says she gets just "zero to three hours" of sleep per night. NPR's Michel Martin asks Johns Hopkins' Dr. Sara Benjamin how much sleep most people need to get through the day.

item.title: Get into med school in the graphic memoir 'See One, Do One, Teach One'
item.description: Grace Farris' book brings readers behind the med school scenes — documenting anxiety over loans, bouts of impostor syndrome, friendships forged in stress, and the ever-impossible work-life balance.

item.title: Why health officials do not have a good handle on the current Ebola outbreak
item.description: To get slightly ahead of the virus, health officials need to quickly identify people at risk of infection, a practice known as contact tracing. That's a challenge in the Democratic Republic of Congo.

item.title: Number of cyclosporiasis cases in the U.S. has surpassed previous records, CDC says
item.description: It can take weeks to confirm a single case of intestinal illness caused by the cyclospora parasite, but the CDC's tally for this year now stands at over 4,100.

item.title: FDA panel supports broadening access to peptides popular on the gray market
item.description: Advisers to the Food and Drug Administration voted in favor of easing regulation of popular peptides. The recommendations could pave the way for specialized pharmacies to produce them in the U.S.
